description_good: README.en.md describes Tsu Swico: a Windows tool that checks Windows and Office licensing and collects a hardware inventory into HTML/XLSX/JSON reports, with data never leaving the machine: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/README.en.md
interact: README.en.md and CONTRIBUTING.md explain how to get the source and binaries, report bugs (issue forms), request features and contribute: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the pull request process: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements: xUnit tests for every change, zero-warning build (TreatWarningsAsErrors, .NET analyzers latest-recommended), Conventional Commits: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
documentation_basics: README.en.md covers installation (winget, Scoop, installer, portable), usage and report contents; docs/ holds architecture, updates and versioning: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_interface: The command-line options are documented in README.en.md and printed by --help (src/Tsudev.Audit.Core/Cli/CliOptions.cs): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/src/Tsudev.Audit.Core/Cli/CliOptions.cs
sites_https: Project site https://swico.tsudev.com and the GitHub repository/releases are HTTPS only.
discussion: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/issues
english: English documentation and bug reports are accepted: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/README.en.md
maintained: Actively maintained, regular commits in November 2026: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/commits/main
repo_track: Git tracks every change with author and date.
repo_interim: Work in progress is pushed to branches and pull requests between releases.
version_unique: Each release has a unique version and git tag: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/tags
version_semver: Calendar Versioning (YY.M.DD with a build counter), documented in docs/VERSIONING.md: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/docs/VERSIONING.md
release_notes: CHANGELOG.md summarises each release in human-readable form: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release so far.
report_process: Bug reports use GitHub Issues with an issue form: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/issues/new/choose
report_responses: No external bug report has been filed so far; the maintainer reads every issue and acknowledges reports within days.
enhancement_responses: No external enhancement request has been filed so far; the feature request form routes them to the maintainer, who answers each one.
report_archive: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process: SECURITY.md explains how to report vulnerabilities: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to a reply within 7 days and a fix for critical issues within 30 days.
build: dotnet build builds the solution; build.ps1 and the release workflow produce the installer and portable package on GitHub Actions: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
build_floss_tools: The .NET SDK and Inno Setup are FLOSS.
test: An automated xUnit suite (188 tests: license verdicts, detection rules, parsers, risk scoring, HTML/XLSX rendering, update checks) is in tests/unittests: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/tree/main/tests/unittests
test_most: Logic is kept in the platform-independent core library precisely so that tests cover it (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md rule 1): verdicts, rules, parsing, scoring, rendering and the update checker are all tested.
test_continuous_integration: GitHub Actions builds and tests on Linux and Windows for every push and pull request: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for every new feature or bug fix: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added: Recent changes added tests with the code, e.g. numeric column alignment came with Cot_so_can_phai_cot_dinh_danh_can_trai (PR #26): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/pull/26
tests_documented_added: The test policy is written in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings: The .NET analyzers run at AnalysisLevel latest-recommended with nullable reference types: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/Directory.Build.props
warnings_fixed: TreatWarningsAsErrors is on, so the build fails on any warning; main builds with zero warnings.
warnings_strict: TreatWarningsAsErrors with latest-recommended analyzers and nullable enabled.
know_secure_design: Design rules keep all network code in one file (UpdateAdapters.cs), all JSON in one serializer, and HTML escaping as the single injection barrier; PRIVACY.md and docs/UPDATES.md document the data flows and the update verification: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/docs/UPDATES.md
know_common_errors: Mitigated errors are documented with code: HTML injection in reports (single escaping barrier + CSP in sample reports), running an unverified downloaded executable (SHA-256 check before launch), leaking machine data (no telemetry, only one network call): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
crypto_published: Only published algorithms: SHA-256 for update verification and TLS (via the operating system) for HTTPS.
crypto_call: The program calls .NET System.Security.Cryptography and the platform TLS stack; it implements no cryptography itself.
crypto_floss: SHA-256 and TLS are implementable with FLOSS (.NET runtime is FLOSS).
crypto_keylength: TLS key lengths are the operating system defaults (TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites); no custom keys are used.
crypto_working: No broken algorithms are used; integrity relies on SHA-256.
crypto_weaknesses: No SHA-1, MD5 or other weak algorithm is used for security.
crypto_pfs: HTTPS uses the platform TLS stack, which negotiates ECDHE (forward secrecy).
crypto_random: The program generates no keys or nonces.
delivery_mitm: Releases are delivered over HTTPS from GitHub; SHA256SUMS.txt is signed with Sigstore (cosign) and builds carry GitHub artifact attestations; the updater verifies the SHA-256 before running an update.
delivery_unsigned: Hashes are only retrieved over HTTPS from the same GitHub release, never over plain HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: No unpatched vulnerability of medium or higher severity: 0 open Dependabot alerts; Dependabot watches NuGet, npm and GitHub Actions.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No critical vulnerability has been reported.
no_leaked_credentials: The repository contains no credentials; signing uses OIDC (keyless Sigstore) and GitHub secrets, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled for the organization.
static_analysis: Roslyn .NET analyzers (latest-recommended, warnings as errors) on every build, and GitHub CodeQL code scanning: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsuswico/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities: CodeQL security queries and the .NET security analyzers (CA2xxx/CA5xxx) look for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed: No medium or higher severity code vulnerability found by static analysis remains open.
static_analysis_often: Static analysis runs on every build, push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis: No fuzzing or other dynamic analysis tool is run yet; the 188 unit tests exercise parsers and renderers with crafted malicious inputs (e.g. HTML injection tests).
dynamic_analysis_unsafe: The program is written in C#, a memory-safe language.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: No dynamic analysis runs yet (see dynamic_analysis).
dynamic_analysis_fixed: No dynamic analysis has been run, so no issue was discovered by it.
